name: How do whole-home renovations handle outdated electrical and plumbing systems?

mainEntity.name: Should electrical and plumbing systems be replaced during a whole-home renovation, even if they still work?
mainEntity.text: Should electrical and plumbing systems be replaced during a whole-home renovation, even if they still work?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whole-home renovations create the best opportunity to modernize hidden systems. Even if old electrical or plumbing still functions, it may not support modern loads, new appliances, or improved fixtures well. Replacing these systems while walls and floors are open can reduce future maintenance and improve safety and reliability. It can also prevent repeated demolition later if those systems fail after the remodel is complete. The decision should be based on age, condition, capacity, and access. A qualified contractor can help determine whether selective replacement is enough or whether a full update is the smarter long-term investment.
acceptedAnswer.description: If electrical or plumbing systems are old, undersized, or difficult to access, replacing them during a whole-home renovation is often more efficient than patching them later. Doing the work while walls are open can reduce future disruption and help avoid repeated repairs.
